sentences.text:
Somarapu Vidyasagar vs The Government Of Telangana on 4
November, 2024

entities.text: Somarapu Vidyasagar vs The Government Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Author: T. Vinod Kumar
Bench: T. Vinod Kumar
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice T. Vinod Kumar
 Writ Petition No.30477 of 2024
Order:

Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing for respondent Nos.1, 2, 4 and 5 and Sri V.Narasimha Goud, learned Standing Counsel,
appearing for respondent No.3 and with the consent of the learned counsel appearing for the parties, the Writ Petition is taken up for hearing and disposal at the admission stage.

2. The case of the petitioner, in brief, is that respondent Nos.2 to 5 are trying to make a layout in petitioner's land admeasuring an extent of Ac.1.20 guntas in Sy.No.102/1 of Hakeempet Village,
Golkonda Mandal, presently Shaikpet Mandal, Hyderabad District, without issuing any notice and without following due process of law under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, as being illegal, arbitrary and violative of Articles 14, 15, 16, 21 and 300-A of the Constitution of India.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
3. Per contra, learned Government Pleader appearing on behalf of respondent Nos.1, 2, 4 and 5 submits that the land being claimed by the petitioner in T.S.No.5 situated at Hakeempet Village, is part of Government land; that an extent of land Acs.52.10 guntas was handed over by the Government to the 3rd respondent for making the same into layout; that the respondents-authorities are undertaking development activity in the aforesaid land handed over to the 3rd respondent; and that the respondents-authorities are not making layout in any other land,
other than the land that has been handed over to the 3rd respondent by the revenue authorities under cover of Panchanama.
4. I have taken note of the respective contentions urged.
5. Though the petitioner claims to be possessor and owner of land admeasuring Ac.1.20 guntas in Sy.No.102/1 of Hakeempet Village, and is cultivating the said land for over 80 years, the document,
on the basis of which the petitioner is claiming the subject land as having been possessed by him,
mentions that the subject land being given as inam by the erstwhile Nizam's Sarfikhas in favour of Smt.Sadamma Jogan for her maintenance by undertaking cultivation.

6. Further, it is to be noted that on abolition of inams, the subject land covered by the aforesaid inam stated to have been given on 13th Isfundah, 1355 Fasli (1945), stood abolished and vested with Somarapu Vidyasagar vs The Government Of Telangana on 4 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3808947/
1 the Government.

entities.text: Somarapu Vidyasagar vs The Government Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
7. Though the petitioner claims to be the legal heir of Somarapu Lingamaiah and undertaking cultivation of the said land, notice dt.08.06.1982 issued by the 5th respondent under the provisions of Section 7 of the A.P. Land Encroachment Act, III of 1905, shows the said Lingamaiah being in unauthorized occupation of the land in Sy.No.102/1 to an extent of Acs.2.00 and the said authority having called upon the said Lingamaiah to submit his explanation within 15 days as to why the said Lingamaiah should not be evicted from the land and forfeiture of the crops, products, buildings,
constructions and things deposited thereon in terms of Section 6 of the Act.

entities.text: A.P. Land Encroachment Act, III of 1905
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 8. Since, the respondents-authorities having issued notice to S.Lingamaiah, who is the father of the petitioner in June, 1982 itself declaring him as an encroacher, the petitioner in absence of placing any material to show that the proceeding initiated under A.P. Land Encroachment Act, 1905 having been adjudicated in favour of his father, cannot claim the subject land as belonging to him and the respondents- authorities are undertaking the act of making layout without following due process of law.

9. Further, in the absence of the petitioner being declared as the owner, possessor or enjoyer of the subject land in the revenue records as filed before this Court to substantiate the aforesaid claim being made by the present petition, this Court is of the view that the petitioner has not established his title to the subject property for restraining the respondents from undertaking development of the land admeasuring Acs.52.10 guntas handed over to the 3rd respondent authority by the concerned revenue authorities and earmarked for making a layout.
10. Thus, the present Writ Petition as filed lacks merit and it is accordingly dismissed.
11. Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this writ petition shall stand closed.

T. VINOD KUMAR, J Date:04.11.2024 GJ Somarapu Vidyasagar vs The Government Of Telangana on 4 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3808947/
